column1: # kit.tsv (harbor#1436) — what a repo of each kind inherits, and whether yard vendors it.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. T18.1 to T18.12 built registers, controls, checks and pins, and a new repo got the naming package
# only: yard vendored 14 files and nothing said what the rest was for. One row per item says which repo kinds carry it,
# which share it belongs to, and whether yard copies it into the repo. `bin/standard-kit.sh --render <kind>` prints a
# kind's items, yard renders exactly those, `--carries <repo>` holds a repo to its kind's list, and a register or a
# control family with no row here is red (standard.kit-complete). bin/standard-vendor.sh builds its package from the
# vendored=yes rows, so "yard vendors it" is this file and not a second list.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> item <TAB> ref <TAB> kinds <TAB> share <TAB> vendored <TAB> note
#   item      register (ref: a path in schemas.tsv) | control (ref: a family, the id's first word, in controls.tsv) |
#             tool (ref: a harbor file a repo runs) | check (ref: the repo's check register fragment) |
#             template (ref: a file yard renders in the repo) | pin (ref: an axis of versions.tsv)
#   kinds     space-separated repo-kinds.tsv ids that inherit the item, or * for every kind
#   share     core (every system built from the core share, installed by harbor deploy) | hub (the platform repos: the control plane,
#             the scaffolder and the fleet controller) | workload (the repos a team writes) | personal (one operator's own layer)
#   vendored  yes when yard copies the item into the repo (a register file, a tool), no when the repo reaches it another way
